No actions this turn. Before I write the design, one bigger choice needs your pick.

This is a project, not a small change. The design will be a full written document in the repository's `specs/` folder, and a reviewer will read it before you do. It must settle how the guide is built, and so far we have only picked how recordings are cleaned up.

**What I found:** the museum's site is made of fixed pages. Nothing on it can receive a file today. So the volunteers' upload path is new work, whichever way we go.

**Two ways to build the guide:**

1. **Everything lives in the existing website.** Each code opens a page on the museum's site, such as `/guide/anchor-chain`. Volunteers sign in to a simple editing screen, such as Decap CMS, and attach their recording. Each upload triggers a site rebuild, and the rebuild cleans up the audio. There is no new service and almost no running cost. The trade-off is that a new recording takes a few minutes to go live, and the audio files are kept with the site's files.
2. **The website plays audio kept in a separate storage service.** The guide pages stay on the site. Volunteers use a small upload page, and the storage service cleans up each file and serves it. Recordings go live almost at once and stay out of the site's files. The trade-off is a second system with its own account, bill and upkeep.

I dropped a phone app. Asking a visitor to install something in front of an exhibit loses most of them.

**I recommend 1.** At ten new recordings a year, a few minutes' delay does not matter. It also keeps one system for the museum to look after.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- On a fixed-page site, "processing" can run at build time instead of on a server. That is why option 1 needs no new service.
- About 120 two-minute files is small enough to keep with the site. At thousands of files, option 2 would win.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Which way do you want to go?
